text:
ConocoPhillips fell 0.23% today to $125.15, extending a two-week decline of 5.58%. The move reflects weakness in crude oil prices: US oil fell to $96.16 per barrel, down from the mid-$128 range where the stock was trading less than a week ago. Saudi Arabia's restoration of Red Sea pipeline flows to 3.5 million barrels per day has eased supply concerns, and broader recovery in crude exports through the Strait of Hormuz has reduced the geopolitical premium that had been supporting prices.

The stock's decline also sits against uncertainty on policy. Trump's recent comments about a potential diesel export ban and ongoing diplomatic signals around Iran sanctions create conflicting signals for energy markets—tighter supply rules could support margins, but near-term policy unpredictability often weighs on large-cap oil stocks until direction becomes clearer.
